t.3.50.1: Bṛhadaśva said: There was a king named Nala, the mighty son of Vīrasena, endowed with desirable virtues, handsome, and skilled in the knowledge of horses.
t.3.50.2: He stood at the head of the lords of men like the lord of the gods, high above them all, like the sun in his splendor.
t.3.50.3: Devoted to brahmins, learned in the Vedas, a hero, a lord of the earth among the Niṣadhas, fond of dice, a speaker of truth, he was a great commander of an akṣauhiṇī army.
t.3.50.4: He was desired by the finest of women, noble-minded, with his senses restrained; a protector, the best of archers, as if he were Manu himself in visible form.
t.3.50.5: Likewise, among the Vidarbhas there lived Bhīma, of terrible prowess, a hero endowed with every virtue; he longed for offspring, yet he was childless.
t.3.50.6: With his mind fully composed, he made the utmost effort for the sake of offspring. To him there came a brahmin seer named Damana, O Bhārata.
t.3.50.7: Desirous of offspring, Bhīma, knower of dharma, together with his queen, pleased that radiant one with honorable hospitality, O lord of kings.
t.3.50.8: Pleased, the greatly renowned Damana granted him and his wife a boon: a jewel of a daughter and three noble sons.
t.3.50.9: Damayantī, and Dama, Dānta, and the radiant Damana, who were endowed with every virtue, formidable, and of formidable prowess.
t.3.50.10: But Damayantī, the slender-waisted one, won renown throughout the worlds for her beauty, her radiance, her glory, her splendor, and her good fortune.
t.3.50.11: Then, when she had reached the proper age, a hundred handmaidens and a hundred female companions waited upon her, richly adorned, as they wait upon Śacī.
t.3.50.12: There Bhaimī, adorned with every ornament, flawless of limb, shone in the midst of her friends like lightning flashing from the clouds; exceedingly endowed with beauty, wide-eyed, she was like Śrī herself.
t.3.50.13: Neither among the gods nor among the Yakṣas, nor among men or others, has such a beautiful woman ever been seen or even heard of before. The lovely maiden is one who agitates the minds even of the gods.
t.3.50.14: And Nala, a tiger among men, unequalled in beauty on earth, was in his beauty like Kandarpa himself become embodied.
t.3.50.16: As the two of them constantly heard of each other's virtues, a love arose between them though they had never seen each other, and that love, O Kaunteya, grew ever greater in their hearts.
t.3.50.15: In her presence they praised Nala out of eager curiosity, and in the presence of the Naiṣadha they praised Damayantī again and again.
t.3.50.17: Then Nala, unable to contain the desire in his heart, went into seclusion and sat in a grove near the women's quarters.
t.3.50.18: Then he saw some geese adorned with golden wings, and of those birds wandering in the forest he caught one.
t.3.50.19: Then the sky-goer spoke words to Nala: "I am not to be killed by you, O king, for I will do what is dear to you."
t.3.50.20: In the presence of Damayantī I shall speak of you, O Naiṣadha, in such a way that she will never think of any man other than you.
t.3.50.21: Thus addressed, the lord of the earth then released the swan; and those swans, flying up, then went to the Vidarbhas.
t.3.50.22: Having gone to the city of Vidarbha, those winged ones then alighted near Damayantī, and she then saw those birds.
t.3.50.23: Seeing those birds of wondrous form, she, surrounded by her band of friends, was delighted, and in haste she set about catching the sky-goers.
t.3.50.24: Then the swans scattered in every direction throughout the pleasure grove, and the maidens ran after those swans, each pursuing one.
t.3.50.25: But the swan that Damayantī had run up to, close at hand, assumed a human voice and then spoke to Damayantī.
t.3.50.26: O Damayantī, there is a king among the Niṣadhas named Nala; in beauty he is like the two Aśvins, and no men are his equal.
t.3.50.27: If you were to become his wife, O fair-complexioned one, then your birth would bear fruit, and this beauty of yours too, O slender-waisted one.
t.3.50.28: For we have seen gods, gandharvas, men, serpents and rākṣasas, yet never before has one such as this been seen by us.
t.3.50.29: You too are a jewel among women, and Nala is the best among men; the union of a distinguished woman with a distinguished man would be excellent.
t.3.50.30: Thus addressed by the swan, O lord of the people, Damayantī then said to that swan, "Speak thus to Nala as well."
t.3.50.31: Having said "So be it" to the daughter of the Vaidarbha king, O lord of the people, the egg-born bird returned to the Niṣadhas and reported everything to Nala.
